brief: GS flags narrow US equity breadth: cap-weighted S&P and NDX keep hitting higher highs while equal-weight S&P has fallen seven straight weeks, because Magnificent Seven earnings strength (META +25% in a month on an agentic-AI consumer thesis, MU rallying despite a stretched multiple, NVDA lifting its buyback to $235bn) keeps pulling capital into mega-cap tech even as 10-year UST yields rose 82bps this quarter. The desk frames the open Q4 question as whether this tech leadership can stay 'duration resistant' against higher rates. It separately argues the technical setup is constructive: quarter-end supply has cleared, long-only and levered funds have cut length, buybacks should resume as Q3 earnings land, and retail was inactive in September, though the index sits near 7700. Momentum as a factor was volatile (-30% July, -14% August, +27% September), so trend-following the obvious leaders is harder than it looks. Elsewhere: Asian equities remain underweight despite price targets implying ~90% upside; Japan's TOPIX and Nikkei have outperformed the S&P year-to-date; Iran talks show no progress and tensions may be rising, though Gulf oil exports are back near 2025 levels; foreign investors keep buying US equities despite de-dollarization talk.
